item.title: Wheelie bins permanently left on pavement – 7 and 9 Millmark Grove, 25th November
item.description:
The households at 7 and 9 Millmark Grove leave their wheelie bins on the pavement all week, not just on collection day. Both properties have space to keep the bins on their own land. The bins narrow the pavement near the junction. Recently someone pushing a pram had to step into the road to get past them. This has already been reported through Love Clean Streets and directly to the council [add reference numbers if you have them], but nothing has changed. Please could the council send both households an advisory letter asking them to store their bins on their property between collections?

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Millmark Grove, New Cross, Greater London

item.title: Dangerous leaves on road and pavements, 25th November
item.description:
The whole of Derwent Road , this is the road and pavements require sweeping. The whole road has many trees in it and the leaves have now all fallen and are covering the road and the pavements making it dangerous for cars and pedestrians alike. This road has not been swept properly for months. We have a man in a truck come down the middle of the road and it cleans the middle of the road, but it does not do the gutters these are chuckle block with leaves and mud there are drains nearby and eventually the leaves will block the drains. This road and pavements require actual bodies with brooms to sweep rather than the machine that only picks up what’s in the middle of the road. Derwent Road has always been neglected, please can this be sorted out
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 10, Malvern Close, Anerley, Greater London
